title: Black Iron Remoulade Cod Plates
seoTitle: Black Iron Remoulade Cod Plates | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Cod on the grill—Cajun blackened char, not fried, hall portions for ten
subtitle: Blackened cod fillets, remoulade, and char for ten
description: Cod fillets coat in Cajun blackening spice, grill in cast-iron griddle inserts until charred and 145°F, and serve with cool remoulade and lemon.

steps.title: Build remoulade
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, Creole mustard, relish, and cayenne. Chill until service. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use mayonnaise as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Season cod
steps.instruction: Pat fillets completely dry. Press Cajun spice, paprika, and garlic powder onto both sides. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Heat cast iron on grill
steps.instruction: Place cast-iron insert on grill and preheat to 425°F, about 10 minutes. Have clarified butter ready. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Blacken first side
steps.instruction: Brush iron with butter. Lay fillets and cook 4 minutes undisturbed until blackened crust forms. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.instruction: Flip carefully and cook 3–4 minutes until 145°F internal and flesh flakes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest before plating
steps.instruction: Rest fillets 2 minutes off heat. Transfer to hotel pans flesh-side up. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 140°F
steps.instruction: Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes max. Remoulade on the side. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve one fillet per firefighter with remoulade and lemon. Call it fast—cod waits poorly. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Dry fillets are mandatory—wet fish won't blacken.
Don't move fillets during first side—crust releases when ready.
Cast-iron insert on grill mimics blackening without indoor smoke.
tonightSpread: Cajun grilled cod with remoulade and lemon.
Dirty rice or hushpuppy-style cornbread on the side.
leftovers: Chop into Cajun fish tacos with slaw.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Grilled blackened cod is a Louisiana lane that uses freezer-case fish every hall already stocks. Fillets cook in minutes on a griddle insert and hold at 140°F briefly.
mealPrepNotes: Pat fillets dry. Grill on cast-iron insert at 425°F, 4 minutes per side. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes. Remoulade cold on the side.
